recipes.name: Classic Cinnamon Rolls
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup warm water (100 to 110 degrees F)
8.5 cups all-purpose flour, or more if needed
1.5 teaspoons Spice Islands® Ground Saigon Cinnamon
1 teaspoon Spice Islands® 100% Pure Bourbon Vanilla Extract
5 tablespoons milk, or more as needed

steps.text: Combine potatoes, potato water, butter, sugar, salt and hot water in large mixing bowl. Stir until butter melts; set aside and let cool. Combine yeast and 1/2 cup warm water in small bowl. Let rest 5 minutes. Add eggs, 2 cups flour and yeast mixture to potato mixture. Beat until well mixed. Continue adding flour, 1 cup at a time until soft dough forms.
Knead on a lightly floured surface until smooth and elastic (about 4 to 6 minutes), OR knead with electric mixer using dough hook. Place in a greased bowl, turning to coat. Cover.
Let rise in a warm, draft free area about 1 hour, until doubled in size. Punch dough down; divide in half.

Roll one portion of dough on a lightly floured surface to a 12 x 18-inch rectangle. Spread with half the butter. Combine sugar and cinnamon; sprinkle half of the mixture over surface. Roll up tightly lengthwise, sealing edges. Cut into 12 slices. Place in greased 13 x 9-inch pan. Repeat with remaining dough. Cover.
Let rise 30 to 45 minutes until nearly doubled.
Bake in preheated 350 degrees F oven for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cool for 15 minutes. Combine icing ingredients and drizzle over rolls.

review.reviewBody: I've never rated before, but this recipe is too good to go without stars! These were so light and delicious, not heavy. I was worried because the dough was so soft, but they came out perfect. Nect time I'll add more cinnamon, that's literally the only flaw!

I love this recipe, and my husband says he likes it more than Cinnabon! Recently I tried making mini rolls, so here are my notes on that: -I halved the size of the rolls, so I assumed I would have 48 rolls instead of 24. I got to 40 mini rolls with just half the dough, so adjust the amount of dough you prep if needed. -All of the other prep is essentially the same up to the cutting and rolling. I added extra cinnamon. -Rolling the dough: Take half of the dough as the og recipe states. Roll it out to be 6 inches wide and 36 inches long. Fill and roll up as original recipe states. -Cutting: I cut each roll to be roughly an inch tall. I think most of then were closer to 3/4 inch. -When putting into pan to rise: grease pan AND put parchment paper. I recommend basting the sides of the rolls with butter as you put them in as well. I crammed more rolls in since they fit better small, but they expanded into each other and made one big cake of rolls, and since they were so small they were hard to separate. -Bake time: 20-25 minutes

Dough only is fabulous!! Made this with my kitchenaid stand mixer and used the kneading attachment and it worked great. I changed the filling to 1 cup packed light brown sugar, 1 cup softened butter, 3 T cinnamon- blend together then spread over the dough evenly. I used Chef Johns cream cheese frosting and these are always gone immediately. **hint- do NOT try to double the recipe; I learned the hard way and cleaned up far too much flour from my floors lol.

I made half the recipe. Also, added more cinnamon as per other reviewers. They are correct! Now, I had to make this recipe into a childhood memory or as close to it, so I did not make the glaze but instead, I added was raisins soaked in rum to the filling. I had also to add more flour about an extra cup to be able to handle it. Still, the dough came out fluffy and soft. It is like a cloud! Also, after baking for 20 minutes, I brushed 4tbsp of melted butter and sprinkled the dough with a mixture of 1 1/2 tbsp granulated sugar, 1 1/2 tbsp of brown sugar, and a bit more cinnamon. Put them in the oven for the last 5 to 10 minutes to check for browning. Let it cool off. The dough is fantastic and the flavor with those additions...was very, very close to my childhood memory of a sweet bread my dad used to bring me after he was done with his shift in the hospital. I will always keep that memory and this recipe just got me closer to revive the sweet, simple, and humble times I lived when having that little sweet bread! WILL ABSOLUTELY MAKE IT AGAIN.

I finally found a recipe that tastes just like my mom’s cinnamon buns! I used vegan butter for spreading and almond milk in the icing. I created a loaf with the uneven pieces from the rolls. I didn’t realize it was going to rise so much and create so much dough- the whole family and the dance teacher got some delivered. Chef’s kiss!

I've made this recipe several times, and just finished another batch. Yes, I made the dough as written. Like others, I opted for brown sugar in the filling and made extra. I used the mixer to combine the softened butter, brown sugar and cinnamon.
The first 1/2 of dough I rolled out and spread the filling on. Yes it was difficult to spread and took some time. For the second 1/2 of the dough I decided to soften the mixture a bit more. I put it in a small bowl in the microwave on 50% power for 10 seconds. NOT to melt it, but to soften and keep the sugar granulated. Doing this made spreading much faster and easier. Also when rolling the down I found it much smoother to roll the second time.
My second tip is to roll the log onto floured wax paper. Roll up and slide on cookie sheet. I refrigerated the dough for 15-20 minutes and the rolls were so much easier to cut!
Love the recipe and recommend it often.

Great recipe. Only thing I did differently is use my bread machine on dough setting. I always do that. I halved recipe to fit plus I didn’t need that many rolls! I am trying mother batch to take to my class later today. Going to make them smaller and letting rise on large jelly roll pan. I used Bakers Cinnamon filling mix from Kung Arthur Flour. Best stuff ever for inside rolls like these. Nice recipe with my little tweak.

These cinnamon rolls are amazing! I bake for a living and am also a licensed Medical Marijuana patient/caregiver. The only substitutions I made were to use green butter instead of regular butter, brown sugar in place of the white in the filling, and if you can find "roasted" cinnamon, I suggest using at least a Tbs. I've made them in 2 pans like suggested, 2 side by side in a loaf pan and 24 individuals in pot pie tins. It's a very flexible recipe and always turns out fantastic!

This is a good basic recipe. I did swap out scalded milk for the water, simply because I like the softer crumb that comes from using milk. But there's not enough cinnamon sugar for the filling. Next time, I will melt the butter, brush it over the rolled-out dough and use double the cinnamon and sugar. I topped it with cream cheese frosting, because I prefer that to powdered sugar glaze.

I've been making these rolls for over 13 years. Now it's a family tradition: Christmas, potlucks, birthdays, any ole occasion. Sometimes I sub sweet potatoes and they come out the coolest color. Double the cinnamon filling and add a little cardamom in the mix, bake in an oversize lasagna pan. We're cream cheese frosting team. The best!

4 stars for the dough, 2 stars for everything else. These taste more like dinner rolls than cinnamon rolls! I doubled the cinnamon and still could hardly see or taste it. The icing is fairly standard. By cooking this size of a batch in 9x13 baking dishes you will get rolls that are a full 2-1/2 inches tall. Far too large to fit into a normal human mouth. If you make this recipe in a 9x13 dish be prepared to eat these with a fork. The dough is actually pretty good. There's not near enough of the cinnamon filling though. I would double the butter and sugar in the filling, and use 4-6 times as much cinnamon. Instead of 1" slices I'd go closer to 3/4" and bake the rolls on a cookie sheet. The thinner rolls will cook faster so the top doesn't dry out as much, and you'll be able to fit them in your mouth!
Made these for the family and they loved them. I used a different icing recipe because I prefer a cream cheese icing on cinnamon rolls
I make these every year during the holidays.
The best cinnamon roll recipe I have made.
Loving it. Works great for rolls.

Fresh out of the oven they were by far the best cinnamon rolls I've ever made!!! The longer they set, next day they were pretty much like other cinnamon rolls I've made. Good but not as good as they were fresh. I will make them again!
So easy to make and every guest at your table will want take some home!

This recipe is not for the beginner, but, it can be done. DO NOT try to cheat with instant potatoes. Also, I never use dough hooks or a mixer. I incorporate flour by hand. Just follow recipe EXACTLY and it will turn out beautifully. Another tip is never overcrowd the pan with more than 12. Even after rising they need to have room to expand. I use cream cheese icing but the actual roll recipe is a keeper.
Amazing! I was told these were so good, I should sell them ! Haha! They freeze great and heat up quick in the microwave on busy mornings. Love this recipe! My kids request it frequently 😀
